ios.desc:
Turn doom scrolling into language learning!

LingoLingo is the easiest way to learn and practice languages. Just start watching, and LingoLingo will learn your preferences and show you engaging YouTube videos that are just right for you! 

Skip videos that are too difficult or if the content isn't for you. Finish videos that you like. Our AI-powered algorithm will learn what kind of videos work best for you and keep you engaged. The easiest and most entertaining way of learning languages - with real content from native speakers!

How it works:

1. Choose your language and start watching
2. Exercises pop up while you watch, to improve your understanding
3. Complete all exercises and celebrate your achievement!
4. Continue and stay engaged with more videos picked just for you!

Choose from 14 languages and level up your vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation and language understanding.

LingoLingo also lets you explore videos in over 20 categories to find content that you love! You can also paste any YouTube link and see the transcript, where you can select words to translate, practice your pronunciation and save new vocabulary. LingoLingo lets you learn with videos made by native speakers. We believe this is the best way to learn - interacting with real content, not with made up sentences and generic topics.

-- Features --
• YouTube Integration: Paste any YouTube link to explore authentic content
• Smart Translations: Get context-aware translations and explanations
• Speaking Practice: Perfect your pronunciation with audio recordings and AI-powered feedback
• Progress Tracking: See exactly how much you've learned
• Final Celebration: Complete your lesson and see your stats!

Install LingoLingo today and start learning languages YOUR way!

android.desc:
Learn Spanish, French, Japanese, German and more with real YouTube videos. LingoLingo turns watching into language practice, with videos picked for your interests and level, word-by-word captions and interactive exercises.

WATCH SOMETHING YOU WANT TO UNDERSTAND
Explore videos from native speakers about topics you enjoy. Personalized recommendations help you find content suited to your level and vocabulary. Practice Spanish listening with everyday conversations, learn French through familiar topics, or discover new Japanese expressions in context.

FOLLOW THE WORDS
Synchronized captions help you follow what's being said. Tap a word for its meaning and pronunciation, then save useful vocabulary to review with flashcards. Reading support such as pinyin, furigana and romaji is available where supported.

PRACTICE WHILE YOU WATCH
Interactive exercises appear during the video to help you check your understanding, connect words with meanings and practice pronunciation. Playback can pause for exercises, giving you time to work through what you've heard.

MAKE ROOM FOR ANOTHER LANGUAGE
Learn German for everyday situations, practice English listening, or explore Italian, Korean and Chinese videos. Whether you're preparing for a trip or following a new interest, build vocabulary from real speech.

LANGUAGES YOU CAN LEARN
English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional options), Greek, Portuguese (Portugal), Russian, Swahili and Turkish.

Choose recommended videos or try a YouTube link. Availability depends on the video's captions, playback restrictions and supported language.

Pick a language, find a video you enjoy and start learning with LingoLingo.

Privacy policy: https://lingolingo.app/privacy-policy

show_hn.title: Show HN: YouTube App Centered Around Language Learning

quotes.text:
Hello HN, here's my app that I built around language learning with YouTube. I'm posting to connect with language learners and people building in this space.

I know some people use YouTube for language learning, but I think it's still a bit under the radar for many. I mean, where else can you find millions of hours of video content with decent quality (mostly) and in virtually every language in existence, about basically any topic there is?

The app has two main goals:
1. Allow interacting with the transcript to copy and translate, which you can't do with the YouTube app.
2. Facilitate interaction with the video content through exercises, to improve understanding and retention.

I'm using it currently to polish up my Mandarin, which I learned to a decent level some 10 years ago. For this kind of casual use case I find it quite good, if I do say so myself.

There's currently around 1k users across Android and iOS. Korean seems to be popular as a target language, as well as Turkish, which interestingly is being learned in Somalia of all places. But according to my stats, it turns out that the most popular language pair is English->English. So right now I'm working on improving the experience for this kind of "monolingual" learning.

The app can be used for free, with an optional ad to unlock exercises per video.

iOS:
https://apps.apple.com/us/app/lingolingo-language-challenge/id6741732641

Android:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.lingolingo.app
